value.
Dithioacetals are versatile synthons frequently used as the
mask of carbonyl groups as well as valuable synthetic
precursors for certain organosulfur compounds in transition
metal catalysis.<sup>10,11</sup> The reactions involving insertion into the
carbon−sulfur bond of dithioacetals provide a privileged
platform for the rapid construction of functionalized
dithioether compounds. Palladium-catalyzed thiol group
migrations, which involve the formal insertion of unsaturated
2π units into the carbon−sulfur bond of dithioacetals, have
already been developed (Scheme 2a).<sup>12</sup> However, these
transformations were limited to only intramolecular processes.

only 1,2-dithioether compounds rather than the desired 1,3-
dithioethers.

aimed for the concurrent introduction of both the thiomethyl
motif and the thiol motif of dithioacetals into allenes in a single
step, similar to the aminomethylamination process using
aminals. Herein, we successfully implemented this idea and
developed a palladium-catalyzed insertion of allenes into
dithioacetals to access
-dithioether compounds (Scheme
2c). Distinguished from previous dithiolation processes, which
solely depended upon the carbon−sulfur bond formation, this
method allowed for the simultaneous construction of one
carbon−carbon bond as well as one carbon−sulfur bond. It
should also be noted that alkyl sulfur sources, which could
hardly be tolerated in preceding dithiolation reactions, were
well amendable to this protocol. This method ofered an
expedient solution for the rapid construction of a variety of
structurally diverse
-dithioethers, which can be used as
valuable synthons and pharmacophores ubiquitously found in
numerous natural products.

and 3t), bromine (3q), and trifluoromethyl (3r), were all
compatible with the reaction conditions. In addition, the
presence of a methyl group at the ortho position of the aryl ring
showed no significant influence on the reactivity of this
transformation, whereas a bulkier chloro substituent evidently
diminished the yield (3u versus 3v). Furthermore, gem-
disubstituted allene 1w was also applicable to this system,
afording corresponding 1,3-dithioether 3w in 68% yield.
Unfortunately, the alkyl-substituted allenes failed to yield any
desired products in our system.
To demonstrate the synthetic potential of this novel
palladium-catalyzed thiomethylthiolation, a large-scale syn-
thetic procedure were conducted. As illustrated in Scheme
the reaction proceeded smoothly on a gram scale when 5.0 mol
% palladium catalyst was used, furnishing corresponding 1,3-
dithioether 3c in 70% yield. Additionally, oxidation of 1,3-
dithioether 3c with 3-chlorobenzoperoxoic acid (m-CPBA)
took place successfully, afording 1,3-disulfone 4 in 62% yield.
The solid structure of 1,3-disulfone 4 was characterized
through X-ray crystallographic analysis.

To gain some insight into the mechanism of this
transformation, a series of control experiments were next
performed. As shown in Scheme 7, treating cationic palladium
Scheme 7. Mechanistic Studies
complex Pd−A with 1.5 equiv of dithioacetal 2a in
dichloromethane (DCM) at room temperature rapidly
produced dithioacetal-coordinated cationic palladium complex
Pd−B (eq 1 in Scheme 7). The solid structure of Pd−B was
unambiguously characterized by X-ray crystallographic anal-
ysis. Subsequently, the standard reaction proceeded smoothly
in the presence of Pd−B, furnishing the desired 1,3-dithioether
product 3a in 56% yield (eq 2 in Scheme 7). These reactions
collectively suggested that dithioacetal-coordinated cationic
palladium complex Pd−B was most likely involved in this
transformation. Furthermore, after 10 min of the standard
reaction, we performed the high-resolution mass spectrometry
(HRMS) analysis of the reaction mixture (eq 3 in Scheme 7),
which detected that alkenyl palladium Pd−C was the main
palladium species (see the Supporting Information for details).
On the basis of the aforementioned mechanistic studies and
previous reports,<sup>16</sup> we proposed a plausible mechanism for the
palladium-catalyzed thiomethylthiolation of allenes with
dithioacetals (Scheme 8). Initially, ligand exchange took
place to form dithioacetal-coordinated cationic palladium
complex Pd−I, which was considered to be the resting state
of this transformation. Upon the decoordination of one
thioether motif of dithioacetal, the terminal carbon−carbon
double bond of allene was able to coordinate to the cationic
Scheme 8. Plausible Reaction Mechanism
palladium complex to form Pd−II. Subsequently, nucleophilic
attack of the decoordinated thioether motif to activated allene
formed alkenyl palladium Pd−III, which was exactly detected
by HRMS analysis. In the meantime, sulfonium species 4a was
formed via carbon−sulfur bond cleavage. Finally, migratory
insertion of sulfonium 4a into the C(sp<sup>2</sup>)−Pd bond took place,
yielding product 1,3-dithioether and regenerating cationic
palladium complex Pd−I through dithioether exchange. The
nucleophilic attack of the C(sp<sup>2</sup>)−Pd bond to sulfonium 4a
also made it possible to complete the catalytic cycle.
In summary, we developed novel palladium-catalyzed
thiomethylthiolations of allenes with dithioacetals, allowing
for the rapid synthesis of a wide range of 1,3-dithioethers. A
unique dithioacetal-coordinated cationic palladium complex
was isolated and characterized, which was considered the
crucial palladium intermediate for this transformation. Further
application and the detailed mechanism of this transformation
are currently ongoing in our laboratory and will be reported in
due course.
